evidence_quotes.quote: The study is a cluster-randomised trial conducted in 100 villages in seven blocks of Puri district in the State of Orissa, India.

Process evaluation data were collected through review of key documentation, quantitative surveys, direct observations, and semi-structured interviews with staff from implementing NGOs and community members.
Table 2 Awareness of mobilisation activities among intervention and control households (n = 807)

In March 2012, a year after implementation, 66% of households in intervention villages were observed to have a completed latrine or one under construction. Coverage was higher among BPL than APL households (68% versus 61%, respectively) and ranged from 54% to 76% across the different NGOs.
implementers decided to provide a subsidy to all households in intervention villages to prevent delays in the implementation.
We found no strong evidence of an association between levels of awareness of or participation in mobilisation activities and levels of latrine coverage in intervention villages.

country.comment: Conducted in seven blocks of Puri district in the State of Orissa, India.
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title and Abstract; PDF p. 3, Results (Study setting)

effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative and qualitative process evaluation findings showing substantial gaps between Total Sanitation Campaign (TSC) guidelines and ground implementation.
effect_estimate.value: Household latrine coverage (completed or under construction) in the 50 intervention villages rose from 8% at baseline (October 2010) to 66% in March 2012 (n = 4,699 households; completed latrines alone rose from 8% to 51% between January 2011 and January 2012, short of the 90% target), with modestly higher coverage among Below Poverty Line (BPL) than Above Poverty Line (APL) households (68% vs. 61%) after subsidies (INR 2,200) were extended to all households regardless of BPL status. Intervention households (n = 408) had higher awareness than control households (n = 399) of the Total Sanitation Campaign (91% vs. 49%, p < 0.001), VWSCs (51% vs. 9%, p < 0.001), wall paintings (44% vs. 7%, p < 0.001) and sanitation home visits in the past 3 months (65% vs. 3%, p < 0.001), but minimal recall of participatory walks/mapping (6% vs. 10%, p = 0.04) or wealth ranking (0% vs. 1%, p = 0.09). Across the 50 intervention villages, village-level latrine coverage showed weak/no association with most mobilisation activities, with modest positive linear regression associations for >=5 VWSC meetings held (coefficient = 0.178, 95% CI: 0.010 to 0.346, p = 0.04), seeing wall paintings (0.171, 95% CI: 0.001 to 0.341, p = 0.05) and receiving a village motivator home visit in the past month (0.216, 95% CI: -0.000 to 0.431, p = 0.05 in Table 4; reported as p = 0.02 in text).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Abstract; PDF p. 4, Results (Latrine construction); PDF p. 6, Figure 1; PDF p. 7-9, Results and Table 2; PDF p. 9, Discussion; PDF p. 11, Table 4

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at 2 under CODEBOOK §9 because the study is appraised as a mixed-methods process evaluation (MMAT). Assigned 2 because field teams directly observed and documented administrative and implementation mechanisms operating on latrine construction over six 6-8 week monitoring rounds (BPL list verification vs. universal subsidy accommodation, household cost-sharing registers, VWSC operations, motivator visits, election code of conduct halts, and subsidy-change disputes).
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF p. 2-7, Methods and Results; PDF p. 9-11, Discussion and Table 4

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines BPL card/Gram Panchayat list eligibility (ELIGIBILITY, documentation), discretionary inclusion of poor non-BPL households via WaterAid/wealth ranking and universal extension of subsidies to all households to avoid community tension (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, hardship_exception, accommodation), household matching material/labour contributions and implementation delays (BURDEN, fees, delay), community complaints over subsidy raises from INR 2,200 to INR 3,200 and sand costs (complaint), VWSCs and PRA mobilisation (participation), local political disputes and a 2-month election code of conduct halt (political_coordination), and door-to-door NGO village motivator support and hardware logistics (bureaucratic_assistance).

mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF p. 3-7, Results (Context, Intervention, Fidelity assessment, Table 1); PDF p. 9-11, Discussion and Table 4

risk_of_bias_tool.comment: Genuine mixed-methods process evaluation combining qualitative methods (semi-structured interviews with NGO motivators and community members, review of activity logs and registers) and quantitative methods (direct latrine observations, random-sample household and VWSC surveys, t-tests, and linear regressions), nested within a parent cluster-randomised trial reported elsewhere.

sample_size.comment: Also includes VWSC formation records from 48 of 50 intervention villages and repeated interviews/record reviews with NGO village motivators across 6 field rounds (25 village motivators and 6 cluster coordinators trained).

study_design.comment: Process evaluation based on the Linnan and Steckler framework conducted alongside a 100-village cluster-randomised controlled trial; combines qualitative interviews/logbook reviews with quantitative household/VWSC surveys, t-tests comparing randomized arms, and village-level linear regressions.
study_design.value: Mixed-methods process evaluation nested within a cluster-randomised controlled trial (combining document review, semi-structured interviews, longitudinal direct observations, quantitative household and committee surveys, and village-level linear regression)
